bills.title: Revise the Ohio Uniform Commercial Code
Ratify the Interstate Compact for School Psychologists
bills.detail: To amend sections 3313.537, 4731.156, and 5903.12; to enact sections 3301.0717, 3301.0733, 3313.5321, 3313.6025, 4731.191, and 4732.42; and to repeal section 4731.155 of the Revised Code to ratify the Interstate Compact for School Psychologists, to modify the Interstate Massage Compact (IMpact), to require, instead of permit, continuing education for massage therapists, regarding the success sequence curriculum, to require the Department of Education and Workforce to submit a report regarding a single, statewide hybrid assessment system, and to enact the Student Athlete Mobility (SAM) Act regarding student petitions to participate in extracurricular activities at neighboring public schools.

bills.title: Enact the Enhanced Cybersecurity for SNAP Act
bills.detail: To amend sections 109.85, 117.10, 2903.216, 2913.40, 2923.31, 4113.52, 5101.542, 5164.32, 5164.33, 5164.36, 5164.57, 5167.03, and 5167.18 and to enact sections 103.413, 3901.93, 5101.5411, 5162.138, 5162.139, 5162.1311, 5162.17, 5162.19, 5162.90, 5163.05, 5164.11, 5164.12, 5164.13, 5164.292, 5164.302, 5164.303, 5164.304, 5164.305, 5164.331, 5164.332, 5164.40, 5164.401, 5164.402, 5164.403, 5164.404, 5164.405, 5164.406, 5164.41, 5164.42, 5164.421, 5164.43, and 5167.23 of the Revised Code regarding program integrity for certain components of the Medicaid program, regarding the authority of the Attorney General and Auditor of State, to require Ohio's SNAP program to begin using chip-enabled EBT cards, and to name section 5101.542 of the Revised Code as amended in this act and section 5101.5411 of the Revised Code as enacted in this act the Enhanced Cybersecurity for SNAP Act and to name the remainder of this act the Ohio Medicaid Program Integrity and Fraud Prevention Act.

label: Week 41, 2026
recap:
This week was quiet, with activity confined to a single jurisdiction. Ohio accounted for all three bill movements, and there were no case updates or federal documents. The bills touched five themes: children and minors, criminal law, health care, transparency and disclosure, and workforce and education. One additional bill movement carried no theme.

The shape of the week was narrow but varied. Three bills moved in Ohio, covering topics from age verification and school use to AI-related offenses, clinical decision support, labeling of AI-generated output, and training programs. No other state or federal activity appeared in the data.

themes.name: Children and minors
themes.blurb: Companion chatbots, age verification, school use, and protections for people under eighteen.

themes.name: Criminal law
themes.blurb: New offenses, penalties, and evidence rules for conduct carried out with AI.

themes.name: Health care
themes.blurb: Clinical decision support, utilization review, mental health chatbots, and AI in diagnosis or coverage decisions.

themes.name: Transparency and disclosure
themes.blurb: Labeling AI-generated output, telling people when they are talking to a machine, and impact assessments.

themes.name: Workforce and education
themes.blurb: Training people to use AI, apprenticeships, curriculum, and public literacy programs.
